info.title: beenfar
info.description:
REST binding of the beenfar controller API. The same operations are
available over Connect, gRPC and gRPC-Web at their protobuf service paths.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (see ApiTokenService) or
with the session cookie set by AuthService.Login.

healthy.title: healthy
healthy.description: Whether the adapter is running (built-in) or connected (external).

statusMessage.title: status_message
statusMessage.description: Last error reported by or about the adapter, if any.

connectTime.title: connect_time
connectTime.description: When the adapter started or last connected.

beenfar.admin.v1.Adapter.title: Adapter
beenfar.admin.v1.Adapter.description: Adapter is a device adapter, such as the built-in UniFi adapter.

beenfar.admin.v1.AdapterKind.title: AdapterKind
beenfar.admin.v1.AdapterKind.description: AdapterKind says where an adapter runs.

beenfar.admin.v1.ApiToken.title: ApiToken
beenfar.admin.v1.ApiToken.description: ApiToken describes an issued bearer token. It never contains the secret.

beenfar.admin.v1.AuthMethod.title: AuthMethod
beenfar.admin.v1.AuthMethod.description: AuthMethod is how a request was authenticated.

passwordLoginEnabled.title: password_login_enabled

oidcProviders.title: oidc_providers
oidcProviders.description: OIDC providers to offer as "sign in with" buttons.

proxy.title: proxy
proxy.description:
Set when a trusted reverse proxy authenticates users. The UI shows no
 login form: an unauthenticated request means the proxy is misconfigured.

basicEnabled.title: basic_enabled
basicEnabled.description:
Whether HTTP Basic auth is accepted (always with API tokens as the
 password; with real passwords only when basic_passwords_enabled).

method.title: method
method.description: How the caller authenticated this request.

imported.title: imported
imported.description: How many devices' keys were stored.

redirectUrl.title: redirect_url
redirectUrl.description:
Where to send the browser next, e.g. the proxy's sign-out page or the
 OIDC provider's end-session endpoint. Empty when there is nothing to do.

id.title: id
id.description: Stable provider id used in URLs, e.g. "corp".

loginUrl.title: login_url
loginUrl.description:
Relative URL that starts the login flow. Append ?redirect=<path> to
 return somewhere other than "/" afterwards.

beenfar.admin.v1.OidcProvider.title: OidcProvider
beenfar.admin.v1.OidcProvider.description: OidcProvider is a configured OpenID Connect identity provider.

logoutUrl.title: logout_url
logoutUrl.description: Where to send the browser to sign out at the proxy, if configured.

currentPassword.title: current_password
currentPassword.description: Required when users change their own password.

mac.title: mac
mac.description: MAC address, in any common notation.

authkey.title: authkey
authkey.description: The device's AES key: 32 hex digits.

gcm.title: gcm
gcm.description:
Whether the device uses AES-GCM. Informational: each inform says how it
 is encrypted, and the reply uses the same.

beenfar.admin.v1.UnifiDeviceKey.title: UnifiDeviceKey
beenfar.admin.v1.UnifiDeviceKey.description:
UnifiDeviceKey is the credential of one UniFi device, as extracted from the
 controller that manages it (its MongoDB "x_authkey", or "mgmt.authkey" in
 the device's /var/etc/persisted/cfg/mgmt).

user.title: user

The full resource. id selects the user; etag, when set, guards the

admin.title: admin
admin.description:
Admins may manage users, every API token and adapters. For external
 users whose provider maps groups to admin, this is derived from their
 groups at each sign-in and cannot be changed here.

source.title: source
source.description: Where the account comes from. External users have no password.

etag.title: etag
etag.description: Opaque version of this resource, for optimistic concurrency.

beenfar.admin.v1.User.description: User is a person who can sign in to the controller.

beenfar.admin.v1.UserSource.title: UserSource
beenfar.admin.v1.UserSource.description: UserSource says where a user account comes from.

beenfar.config.v1.AdoptDeviceRequest.title: AdoptDeviceRequest
beenfar.config.v1.AdoptDeviceRequest.description: At most one of `id`, `mac` may be set.

adapter.description: Name of the adapter that handles this device, e.g. "unifi".

locked.title: locked
locked.description:
The device was seen but its adapter holds no credentials for it, so it
 cannot be adopted yet (for UniFi: it is still managed by another
 controller). Import its credentials, or reset it, and it stops being
 locked the next time it is seen.

beenfar.config.v1.Device.title: Device
beenfar.config.v1.Device.description: Device is a piece of network gear known to the controller.

beenfar.config.v1.DeviceState.title: DeviceState
beenfar.config.v1.DeviceState.description: DeviceState is the adoption state of a device.

state.description: Only return devices in this state. Unspecified returns all.

Gateway address and prefix length in CIDR form, e.g. "192.168.10.1/24".
 Empty for a pure L2 network.

First and last address of the DHCP pool. Required, and inside subnet,

beenfar.config.v1.WifiBand.title: WifiBand
beenfar.config.v1.WifiBand.description: WifiBand selects the radio bands a wireless network is broadcast on.

securityKey.description:
Pre-shared key. Required for WPA personal (8-63 characters, or 64 hex
 digits) and WEP (5 or 13 characters, or 10 or 26 hex digits); must be

 default (untagged) network.

apGroups.description: Access point groups that broadcast this network. Empty means all.

get.description: ListAdapters returns every registered adapter, ordered by name.

post.description:
ImportUnifiDeviceKeys stores the credentials of UniFi devices that
 another controller manages, so that this controller can read their
 informs once they are pointed at it. The devices are recorded as pending
 (with their real model once they have informed) and are adopted, which
 re-keys them, like any other. The keys are never returned by any API.

get.description: ListApiTokens lists the caller's tokens, or every token for an admin.

post.description:
CreateApiToken issues a token for the calling user. The secret is
 returned only in this response; the server keeps only its hash.

get.description:
GetAuthConfig describes the sign-in methods this controller offers, so a
 UI can render the right login screen. It needs no credentials.

post.description:
Login checks a username and password and starts a session. The response
 sets an HttpOnly session cookie. Fails with UNAUTHENTICATED on bad
 credentials.

Logout ends the current session and clears the cookie. When the user
 signed in through an external provider, redirect_url is where the UI
 should send the browser to sign out there too.

get.description: GetCurrentUser returns the user behind the caller's session or token.
ListDevices returns devices, ordered by MAC address.

parameters.description: Only return devices handled by this adapter. Empty returns all.

get.description: GetDevice returns one device by id.

delete.description:
ForgetDevice removes a device, adopted or pending. A forgotten device that
 is still on the network shows up again as pending.

post.description:
AdoptDevice brings a pending device under management. It fails with
 NOT_FOUND if no such device has been seen and FAILED_PRECONDITION if it
 is already adopted.

get.description: ListNetworks returns every network, ordered by name.

post.description: CreateNetwork creates a network. Name and non-zero VLAN ids are unique.

get.description: GetNetwork returns one network by id.

delete.description:
DeleteNetwork deletes a network. It fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION while
 a wireless network still refers to it.

put.description:
UpdateNetwork replaces every mutable field of a network. When etag is
 set it must match the stored etag, or the call fails with ABORTED.

DeleteUser deletes a user with their tokens and sessions. It fails with
 FAILED_PRECONDITION if it would leave no admin.

post.description:
SetUserPassword changes a password. Users changing their own password
 must give the current one; admins resetting another user's need not.
 Every session of the user is ended; API tokens keep working.

tags.name: AdapterService
tags.description: AdapterService reports the device adapters registered with the controller.

tags.name: ApiTokenService
tags.description:
ApiTokenService manages bearer tokens for programmatic access (Terraform,
 scripts). A token acts as the user who created it. Users see and revoke
 their own tokens; admins see and revoke everyone's.

tags.name: UserService
tags.description:
UserService manages controller users. Only admins may call it, except that
 any user may read their own record and change their own password.

tags.name: AuthService
tags.description:
AuthService signs browser users in and out with a session cookie. API
 clients use bearer tokens from ApiTokenService instead.

tags.name: DeviceService
tags.description:
DeviceService manages network devices: discovery results, adoption and
 removal. Devices are created by adapters when they are first seen, in the
 PENDING state; AdoptDevice brings one under management.

tags.name: NetworkService
tags.description: NetworkService manages wired/L3 networks (VLANs and their subnets).
